Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-18

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), planned by Dr. Reyes. The denial letter dated August 18, 2026, states that “the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.” 

This determination is incorrect and directly contradicts the governing medical policy, **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769 for Shoulder Arthroplasty**. As detailed below, my clinical records not only demonstrate that conservative treatment is explicitly waived under your policy due to the severity of my joint disease, but they also document that I have already completed an exhaustive conservative trial that far exceeds the plan's requirements.

### 1. Medical Policy Exception: Conservative Treatment is Not Required
According to the "INDICATIONS" section of Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769 for CPT 23472:
*   "Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)*"
*   "*NOTE: In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required"

**Clinical Evidence:** My shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) obtained on June 4, 2026, demonstrate a "complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid." Because I have documented bone-on-bone articulation, your policy explicitly states that a trial of non-operative treatment is **not required** to establish medical necessity. 

### 2. Full Satisfaction of Conservative Care Criteria (14 Weeks of PT & 6 Months of NSAIDs)
Even if the conservative care requirement were not waived, my records confirm that I have already failed an extensive conservative regimen. The policy requires:
*   "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following:
    ○ Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program
    ○ Rest or activity modification
    ○ Application of heat or ice
    ○ Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics)
    ○ Corticosteroid injections"

**Clinical Evidence:** I have failed three of these modalities over a period exceeding 12 weeks:
*   **Physical Therapy:** I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 12, 2026, to July 19, 2026 (spanning 16 total visits). The therapy was appropriately focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Pharmacologic Treatment:** I utilized oral NSAIDs daily for 6 months, which provided completely inadequate pain relief.
*   **Corticosteroid Injection:** I received an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on June 7, 2026, which yielded only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief.

### 3. Fulfillment of All Other Clinical Requirements
My clinical records satisfy all additional criteria outlined in Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769:
*   **Severe Pain and Functional Limitations:** The policy requires "Evidence of painful osteoarthritis or inflammatory, non-infectious arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid) with functional limitations such as ADLs, employment, or recreation". I have experienced 24 months of progressive, severe pain that is unrelieved by rest. Functionally, I cannot reach overhead, dress myself without assistance, or sleep on my affected side.
*   **Intact Rotator Cuff:** The policy requires a "Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan". A shoulder CT scan performed on June 4, 2026, explicitly confirms that my rotator cuff is fully intact, and my physical examination demonstrates intact rotator cuff strength.
*   **Physical Exam Objective Findings:** My clinical notes document severe physical limitations, including glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to just 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees.
*   **Timing of Prior Injections:** The policy contraindicates surgery if there is "No cortisone injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery". My last injection was on June 7, 2026. The 12-week safety window closed on August 30, 2026. My surgery is planned for [Proposed Surgery Date], which is well beyond this 12-week timeframe.
*   **No Contraindications:** I have no history of prior shoulder infections or shoulder arthroscopic surgeries. I have no active infections, no untreated substance use disorders, a healthy BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

### Conclusion
My clinical presentation and imaging meet every requirement for total shoulder replacement under Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769. I have complete, bone-on-bone joint space loss, meaning conservative treatment is waived under your own guidelines. Furthermore, I have already exhausted 14 weeks of physical therapy, 6 months of NSAIDs, and an injection to no avail. 

I request that Iowa Total Care immediately reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for CPT code 23472. Please contact my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, at [Surgeon Phone Number] or me at the phone number listed above if you require any additional information. 

Sincerely,

Reese Carter
